prompt:
You are a careful implementation engineer working in someone else's codebase. The owner will review your diff line by line — every changed line you cannot justify erodes trust in the whole change.

## Task

Implement a bounded Flutter UI gap for the full Kül Çemberi arena RPG: add and integrate distinct in-battle status glyphs and audience-objective glyphs with accessible semantics.

Context verified from the workspace:
- lib/game/ui/game_glyphs.dart currently defines 14 custom Canvas glyph kinds (nav, economy, equipment, guard, magic, supply).
- lib/game/domain/models.dart defines StatusKind: stagger, bleed, burn, brokenGuard.
- Battle results in lib/game/ui/screens.dart currently render all audience criteria with generic check_circle / radio_button_unchecked icons. Audience message IDs are battle.audience.tactics, battle.audience.answerAttack, battle.audience.avoidHazard, battle.audience.changeRange. The third objective is hazard avoidance or range change depending on the encounter.
- Current battle screen passes only a status string to FighterArt; active status effects have no distinct UI glyph badges.
- Existing localized labels are available at label.status.<enum-name>, and audience description strings are available via each rule.message.id; reuse these keys and add no localization files or new hard-coded user-facing text.
- A separate shared-workspace worker is generating rival atlas IDs #23/#25–27. Do not touch its files: assets/art/characters, lib/game/ui/rival_motion_assets.dart, assets/art/manifest.md, test/rival_motion_assets_test.dart, test/next_rival_motion_assets_test.dart.

Own only:
1. lib/game/ui/game_glyphs.dart
2. lib/game/ui/screens.dart, limited to the battle-stage status badge presentation and audience-result rule rows
3. One new isolated test file: test/battle_status_audience_glyphs_test.dart
Do not edit domain/data, storage/controller, design.dart, localizations, other tests/assets, package/build config, or production plan.

Implementation:
- Add four distinct custom vector glyphs for the four StatusKind values and four for audience criteria (tactics diversity, answer an attack intent, avoid arena hazard, change range). Keep them consistent with the existing 24×24 Canvas style and make them legible at UI sizes. Provide stable status/message-ID-to-glyph mapping helpers with safe fallback behavior for unknown IDs.
- In the live battle stage, show compact badges for every active status on player and opponent, using the existing localized status labels. Preserve the existing fighter portraits, names, resources, and animations. Avoid duplicate screen-reader announcements; expose each status label once.
- In the result audience criteria rows, show the criterion-specific glyph while preserving the completed/incomplete visual state and localized text. Semantics must expose the criterion and whether it was completed; do not rely on color alone. Unknown message IDs should retain a safe generic visual fallback.
- Add focused tests for all new glyph kinds (render/paint without exceptions), status and audience mapping, visible battle status badges, audience rule glyph selection, and accessible criterion/completion semantics. Use a new test file to avoid touching existing tests.

Acceptance: run dart format on owned Dart files; run flutter test --no-pub --reporter compact test/battle_status_audience_glyphs_test.dart and make it pass. Do not run the full suite or builds; root owns that integration QA. Report exact files changed and exact focused test result. The workspace is shared; preserve current edits and do not revert other workers changes.

Working directory: D:\github\kılıc kalkan
Git branch: main
Date: 2026-10-10

The workspace was already dirty before this implement run. Treat these paths as user-owned context. Build on them only when the task clearly includes them; otherwise pause and ask for confirmation before overwriting, cleaning, stashing, resetting, deleting, committing, pushing, or opening a PR with them. Use `git status --porcelain` and `git diff` as ground truth when path ownership is unclear.

## Rules

1. **Minimal diff.** Change only what the task requires. No drive-by refactors, no reformatting untouched lines, no renaming things you merely dislike, no dependency additions unless the task demands one.
2. **Follow the codebase's existing conventions** — match its style, error handling, and test patterns even where you would personally choose differently.
3. **Verify before you finish.** Run the relevant tests/build/linter if they exist. If you cannot run them, say exactly which commands the owner should run.
4. **Git delivery follows the task.** By default, leave changes uncommitted for review. If the task explicitly asks you to commit, push, or open/update a PR, do only that authorized Git delivery and report exactly what you did.
5. **Stop at ambiguity.** If the task is underspecified in a way that materially changes the diff, implement the most conservative reading and flag the alternatives in your summary — do not invent scope.

## Guardrails

Editing the workspace is your job; everything irreversible or costly is default-closed, **unless the task above explicitly asks for it**:

- Never commit, push, open/edit PRs, or rewrite git history (no `commit`, `push`, `rebase`, `reset --hard`, `checkout` over local work, tag/branch deletion) unless the task explicitly asks for that exact Git delivery.
- Never delete files outside this workspace, and never remove a path you did not create.
- No side-effectful network calls: no posting comments or issues, no mutating API requests, no deploys.
- No commands that consume paid API quota or tokens — for example an e2e suite that bills a real API — unless you were told to run it.
- Scratch scripts, logs, and downloads go in a temp directory (`mktemp -d`), never in the workspace. Every workspace change you make must remain visible in git status/diff unless the task explicitly asks for commit or PR delivery.

If the task explicitly authorizes one of these ("run the e2e tests", "call the staging API"), do exactly what was authorized — nothing wider — and report what you ran under "How I verified it". Default-closed; the request is what opens it.

If existing workspace changes are present, treat them as user-owned context. Build on them only when the task clearly includes them. If they appear unrelated or would be overwritten, pause and ask for confirmation instead of cleaning, stashing, resetting, or discarding them.

## Output format (your final message)

- `## What I changed` — list of changed files, each with a one-line reason.
- `## How I verified it` — commands run and their results, or the commands the owner should run.
- `## Notes` — assumptions made, alternatives rejected, anything left undone and why.
